Docs-only typography pass (curly → straight apostrophes) plus two URL updates. Two substantive concerns:

1. The new link in `docs/explanation/security.md:110` is dead. `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019` returns HTTP 404 on the relaunched Ubuntu MediaWiki wiki (legacy pages were not migrated), and the old `help.ubuntu.com/community/...` URL now redirects to that same missing page. Swap to a live reference such as `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/security-features/storage/encryption-full-disk` (verified reachable) instead of only changing hosts. MAAS's own style guide says "Ensure all hyperlinks are functional and relevant".

2. The stated rationale ("proselint compliant") does not hold up. The repo does not run proselint: docs CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `test-docs`) runs `make install`, `make lint-md` (pymarkdownlnt) and `make html`, and `docs/Makefile` only exposes `vale`, `woke`, `spelling`, `lint-md` and `linkcheck`. Proselint's only quotation-related check is `typography.symbols.curly_quotes`, which flags straight double quotes and asks for curly ones; there is no proselint rule against `’`. Meanwhile the overwhelming majority of the docs (e.g. `docs/explanation/deploying-machines.md:19,27,33,42,80`, the Canonical style guide itself) use curly apostrophes, so this change makes these five files typographically inconsistent with the rest of the corpus and produces mixed typography within single sentences. Either keep curly apostrophes or do a repo-wide, tool-backed normalization — a partial per-file conversion adds churn without a verifiable benefit.

The Juju link change is fine: `https://canonical.com/juju` resolves and matches the existing usage in `docs/how-to-guides/get-started/index.md:16`.

docs/explanation/security.md.110: New target is dead: `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Full_Disk_Encryption_Howto_2019` returns HTTP 404 (the old `help.ubuntu.com/community/...` URL now redirects to that same missing page on the relaunched MediaWiki wiki, where legacy pages were not migrated). Point at a live resource, for example `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/security/security-features/storage/encryption-full-disk` (verified reachable), rather than only changing the host.

docs/uncategorized/what-maas-shouldn-t-d.46: This line now mixes typography: a straight apostrophe (`don't`) next to curly double quotes (`“just work.”`). The rest of the docs and Canonical's style guide use curly apostrophes, and proselint's only quote rule (`typography.symbols.curly_quotes`) actually flags straight double quotes and asks for curly ones — it has no rule against `’`. So this conversion doesn't increase proselint compliance; either keep the original apostrophes or normalize quotes/apostrophes repo-wide in one pass.

docs/how-to-guides/manage-machine-groups.424: Inconsistent within the page: this line keeps curly quotes (`“deploy only machines with SSDs”`) while line 430 still has straight double quotes (`"team A can only deploy machines in pool X."`) and the apostrophes here are now straight. Pick one convention and apply it consistently; as written the file mixes three styles and the change itself doesn't resolve any proselint finding (the repo's docs CI runs pymarkdownlnt/Vale, not proselint).
